abi.evidence_scope: Read-only login-node system query supplied by dispatcher; compare allocated-node runtime at proof time
abi.required_headers: Complete matching development include tree, including generated pyconfig.h and dependent cpython/internal subdirectories present in the package. Copying only Python.h is insufficient. Honor distinct include and platform-include directories if present.
abi.qualification: Exact distribution build is preferred and minimizes unknowns. CPython documents same-minor release compatibility when compiled the same way; exact patch equality is not presented as a universal ABI requirement. No fallback build has been accepted.

proposed_minimal_repair: Obtain the matching authentic distribution development package and preserve URL, NEVRA/architecture, repository digest and signature verification evidence. Privately extract, without installing to or changing /usr or the accepted environment archive.

Bind every extracted regular file by relative path/SHA/size, reject unexpected links/paths, and record immutable supplement hash. Verify patchlevel and generated platform configuration against the actual shared interpreter/sysconfig.

Add the private complete include tree to the compiler include search in an explicit reviewed invocation (for example a scoped CPATH), preserving the former runtime environment and source. Do not silently replace the interpreter or disable the native backend.
minimum_cpu_proof: On an authorized zero-GPU compute job, use the same shared interpreter and exact accepted environment. Record interpreter/package/source versions, compiler, sysconfig, selected include tree and library resolution.

Preserve hashes of the installed Torch outer-product files, Triton runtime/build.py, NVIDIA driver.py and driver.c; local Mac Torch source snapshots are supporting evidence, not proof of identical Newton wheel bytes.
Use a fresh isolated TRITON_CACHE_DIR and no pre-existing compiled object. Inspect actual installed driver.c PyInit and build helper signature before choosing a GPU-free import route.

Compile and load the exact installed NVIDIA driver.c through the installed build helper and actual libcuda path, without constructing driver.active or invoking CUDA methods. Capture compile invocation and produced extension hash. If its actual module initializer needs a GPU, report compile-only honestly and defer import to allocated GPU proof.

A minimal separate C-extension ABI probe may additionally report compile-time PY_VERSION, pointer size, Py_DEBUG and Py_GetVersion under the actual interpreter. This supports but does not replace the exact Triton helper build.
Preserve return codes/stdout/stderr and clean only owned temporary outputs. CPU compilation/import is not evidence of a functioning GPU kernel, optimizer or distributed training.
later_gpu_proof: Use a fresh isolated compiler cache and the explicitly bound header supplement under the accepted interpreter, unchanged model/data/config/backend, on an authorized healthy allocated GPU node.

Execute actual competitive head forward, masked loss backward, finite gradients and a real optimizer update; preserve shape/dtype, source/config/weight/supplement hashes, exact operation counters and CUDA synchronization result. The full actual pilot additionally validates the frozen official encoder path.
Then the authorized two-GPU diagnostic continuous/interrupted/resume workflow must pass; an earlier CPU forward or extension import cannot satisfy this gate.
